text.p: Uhispank, the third-largest bank in Estonia, said on Thursday it will revise its 1997 profit forecast after first half results and that revision would be in an upward direction.
Asked by how much the bank would increase its 1997 profit forecast, board member Ulo Suurkask said he would not give any figures for now.

"But when you look at the first five months results, it gives the picture," he said, meaning that the first five months profit was 49.2 million kroons compared with a previous 1997 profit forecast of 105.8 million kroons.
"We will definitely revise the forecast after the first half year results are clear," he added, noting that figures so far were higher than expected.
Suurkask also said it was realistic to exceed the balance sheet estimate of 7.5 billion kroons for 1997.
"We do not see any doubt about it," he said when asked if this was possible.
Uhispank assets in May were at 6.1 billion kroons, growing by 440 million kroons.
